name: Datalog
note: function-free declarative logic for recursive database queries; its deductive-database roots date to 1977, while the name Datalog was coined in the mid-1980s
typeSystem: Classical Datalog is untyped: facts and rules are first-order terms over relations with no function symbols. Particular descendants may add a type system; for example, Soufflé statically checks declared relation-column types and also supports records and algebraic data types.
runtime: A Datalog engine repeatedly applies rules to a database of facts until a fixed point is reached (naive or semi-naive evaluation), then answers queries against the resulting relations.

runtimes.name: Soufflé
runtimes.role: Ahead-of-time compiles Datalog programs to highly optimised C++, used for large-scale static analysis.

runtimes.name: Bottom-up Datalog interpreter
runtimes.role: Directly evaluates rules via naive or semi-naive fixpoint iteration without a separate native-code compilation step.

compilers.name: Soufflé
compilers.role: Compiles Datalog to native C++ for high-performance batch evaluation.

concurrencyModel: N/A in the core declarative language; engines such as Soufflé parallelise fixpoint computation across CPU cores internally.

codeExample.caption: Transitive closure of a parent relation (Soufflé-style)
codeExample.source:
.decl parent(x: symbol, y: symbol)
.decl ancestor(x: symbol, y: symbol)

parent("tom", "bob").
parent("tom", "liz").
parent("bob", "ann").

ancestor(X, Y) :- parent(X, Y).
ancestor(X, Y) :- parent(X, Z), ancestor(Z, Y).

.output ancestor
